title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

body.p: Thy daughter is down with the measles. she has them finely, they began to turn on her last night. I propose leaving her this morning to attend our Quarterly Meeting in care of our Ruth, who with my son I expect shortly to take sick with it. I heard last week all thy children were well. Likewise thy companion’s family were well. Ebenezer Creeson, by whom received the above intelligence, is about trying to purchase a plantation in our neighborhood. Cousin Ruth Walmsley is just recruited from a severe spell of the colic, she has a minute to visit the family of Middleton Monthly Meeting. May her movements in some respects excite us of poor Byberry to more future industry to set our houses in order. We heard trenchantly severely by of your movements, & was enabled to move forward in the line of your duty, which no doubt produces its reward. I hope adequate to the of both body & mind which I apprehend one not few, just so much from a poor unworthy sister. I hope in the written along side of page Near fellowship of the gospel, if I may venture to use the expression.

closer.salute: I salute thee & thy companion, & conclude your affectionate Friend,
